acceptance_mapping.statement: Any byte change creates a new Durable Knowledge Material Object identity.
Object identity includes domain, algorithm version, and digest of exact bytes.
Every operation binds one current namespace, policy version, and storage realization.
A locator may change and may return candidate bytes; only qualified byte verification establishes object identity.
A successful write receipt is not proof of later retrieval, retention, or availability.
A consumer may perform its declared dependent effect only after exact byte and context verification under the current binding.
Absent, unavailable, unauthorized, expired, mismatched, policy-mismatched, or ambiguous results never emit storage success.
Envelope reissue follows write replacement, verify replacement, commit active replacement, then policy-governed retirement of prior bytes.
Provider, adapter, namespace, endpoint, and locator are realization or binding facts, never immutable object identity.
Every storage claim is bounded to the exact realization, binding, policy, environment, and observation interval.
Storage infrastructure cost remains distinct from knowledge price, seller payment, royalty, license consideration, and owner compensation.
Stored or evidenced material may contain encrypted bytes and allowed metadata but never plaintext, unwrapped content keys, private keys, or credentials.
A consumer instantiation names every reuse or specialization and fills every required semantic slot before DomainSpec or implementation binding.

exclusions: selecting a storage provider, adapter, endpoint, region, credential, commercial plan, or deployment
making provider identity, locator syntax, or mutable object name part of immutable byte identity
treating a write receipt, digest, locator, or one successful retrieval as perpetual availability or retention proof
placing plaintext, a content-encryption key, envelope plaintext, recipient private keys, or credentials in stored or public protocol material
claiming cross-system atomicity between storage and a consuming protocol
silently selecting retention, availability, redundancy, migration, deletion, or recovery targets for a consumer
rewriting consumer-capability semantics or treating a consumer instantiation as provider realization
knowledge price, seller payment, royalty, licensing, legal title, reputation, publication, release, deployment, or external execution
capability.outcome: For one exact encrypted Knowledge Artifact Version or recipient-specific key envelope, persist immutable bytes under an exact durable-storage policy, verify retrieval against their qualified content identity before dependent use, and emit environment-bounded evidence without exposing plaintext, keys, credentials, or provider identity as object identity.

limitations: Description import only; PostgreSQL, Docker, archive and recovery tests were not run. Semantic contract identities resolve but do not prove operational restoration.
Credit release, inventory reservation and production rollback remain reference examples, not capabilities.
notes: Product boundary and declared owner completed from its explicit source Product Thesis.
Source lifecycle preserved verbatim; candidate storage does not activate it.
Realization references preserved as unverified source metadata; no realization asserted.

product.identity_boundary: A remains a co-owner when B is added; plaintext and content keys remain outside public protocol state; the protocol does not custody the encrypted artifact; stable identity remains distinct from signing and encryption keys; reissue does not change ownership or economic state; SOL, licensing, royalties, reputation, publication, release, and deployment are excluded
